answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with a portion forfeited when an adjudicated interaction proves fraudulent. Reputation then accrues only from completed exchanges with independently staked counterparties, so an attacker cannot cheaply manufacture trust by having its own identities endorse one another. The stake is an anchor for accountability: creating a swarm means tying up real capital, while each exposed fake risks a slashing ripple through its linked accounts. Nectar alone cannot buy a credible history.
